title: How many placed designs from a new family does an area surrogate need, and does the answer change when the target is placed area instead of a synthesis cell count?
summary: All 133 designs of eda-surrogate (four generator families) are mapped to SKY130 HD with Yosys 0.33 and ABC and placed with the OpenROAD PyPI wheel (placement-based parasitics, repair_timing at 8 ns). The few-shot curves of eda-adapt are refitted to repaired area and to placed period, with the generic cell count as a paired check (it reproduces eda-adapt’s table exactly). With word-level features only, an unseen family’s placed area has a median error of 39% (ridge) or 60% (non-negative linear); one placed design from the new family cuts these to 23% and 27%, and about three reach 20% for most families, the same order as for cell counts. Training on the new family alone overtakes pooling from about three designs; boosted trees need 12 for two families. Period is harder to read: gbr is at 20% with no new design and halves with eight. Limits: placement only (no routing or clock tree), ideal clock, one ABC target, 133 designs from four hand-written generators, no confidence interval over designs; the period target is the placed period of a netlist mapped at a loose 8 ns, not the fastest the design runs.
lede: the eda-adapt few-shot curves refitted to OpenROAD-placed area on 133 SKY130 designs: an unseen family's placed area is off by 39% (ridge), one placed design cuts it to 23%, about three reach 20%, as for cell counts.
